A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SaFiRe research and contain the complete main text, references, and Appendices A–E. Textual and visual inspection supports matching all equations, tables, and figures without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, ablations, and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–7, alongside dataset analyses and qualitative results in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and analyses, including SaFiRe results on the RefCOCO benchmarks and aRefCOCO.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same encoders, alternating Saccade and Fixation operations, group-scan-recover procedure, segmentation head, and Dice/Focal training objective. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training coverage and evaluate RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, and aRefCOCO. The object-distracting and category-implicit scenarios and Appendix D dataset construction are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3 and 7. The qualitative comparisons also retain ReMamber and PSALM in Figures 4 and 7.

E3.justification: The single-dataset and mixed-data evaluations, zero-shot aRefCOCO protocol, and oIoU, mIoU, and Precision@X metrics are unchanged. Both retain the same model configurations, 50-epoch training schedule, and 4 × 4 Fixation windows.

E4.justification: Both retain the module, window-size, and backbone ablations in Tables 4–6, layer-wise feature analysis in Figure 3, and failure cases in Figure 5. Appendix D distribution analyses and Appendix E qualitative examples are also identical.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results are retained. For example, Table 3 reports SaFiRe at 65.1 oIoU and 71.4 mIoU on aRefCOCO in both versions, while Table 7 retains 384 GFLOPs and 8.26 FPS. Appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), including the sequence definitions and Section 3.5 complexity derivation, are unchanged. Equation (3) moves to the following page without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about referential ambiguity, cognitively inspired Saccade–Fixation processing, aRefCOCO, and performance advantages. The added project-page line introduces no scientific claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of module complementarity and Mamba's suitability remain identical. The same failure mechanisms, language-diversity limitations, generated-description biases, and pretrained-encoder biases appear in Sections 4.7–5 and Appendices A–B.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL at the end of the abstract, providing access information absent from v1. Implementation details and dataset-generation instructions remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish what code or data the linked page supplies.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix C are unchanged. Reference [87] changes an author name from 'Y. Yuhuan' to 'Y. Yang', a bibliographic correction rather than a different citation or positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds the project-page line, corrects the author name in reference [87], and updates the arXiv version/date header. The substantive prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Limited text reflow and spacing adjustments affect pages 1–5 and reference [87]; Equation (3), for example, shifts from page 3 to page 4. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–7 retain their content, design, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 makes a small usability and editorial improvement by adding a project-page pointer and correcting attribution in reference [87]. The scientific arguments, experiments, and appendices are unchanged, so the gain is limited to access information and bibliographic accuracy; actual availability of linked resources is not established by the PDFs.
